criteria.quote: Seel hunts under ice. Then its horn punches through.
criteria.revision: Make the first line withhold the purpose while preserving the researched action: “Seel hunts for prey beneath sheets of ice—then punches through it when it needs to breathe.”

criteria.quote: Seel hunts beneath ice, then uses its hard head horn to punch a breathing hole.
How does Seel breathe while hunting beneath sheets of ice?
criteria.revision: Keep this question unanswered until the final reveal by changing the opening narration to: “Seel hunts for prey beneath sheets of ice. But how does it breathe?”

criteria.quote: Under ice, Seel hunts for prey in frigid seas.
criteria.revision: Make the scenes progress from habitat to adaptation to reveal: follow the hunt with “It relishes freezing climates around 14 degrees Fahrenheit,” then “Its horn is very hard—hard enough to bash through thick ice,” and only then reveal that it punches a hole to breathe.

criteria.quote: When it needs to breathe, Seel punches a hole through the ice.
criteria.revision: The research supports no stronger factual twist, so delay this exact reveal until the last substantive scene. Remove “A HOLE FOR AIR” from the headline and use a neutral setup such as “THEN IT NEEDS TO BREATHE,” saving “it punches a hole through the ice” for the narration.

criteria.quote: Its head horn is very hard, built for bashing through thick ice. / When it needs to breathe, Seel punches a hole through the ice. / The same horn that breaks thick ice makes Seel's breathing hole.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated final setup with a distinct researched detail: “While it swims, Seel’s nostrils close.” Then use the next scene for the breathing-hole reveal instead of restating that the horn breaks ice.

criteria.quote: Seel uses its hard head horn to punch through ice when it needs to breathe.
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve the contrast rather than repeat the premise: “Its horn is known for bashing thick ice—but when Seel needs to breathe, that same head point punches a hole through it.”

criteria.quote: Is Seel's horn mainly an ice-breaker or a breathing tool?
criteria.revision: Avoid claiming the research establishes which use is primary. Ask: “Which is the stranger use of Seel’s horn: bashing thick ice, or making a hole to breathe?”
